rules.name: Smooth manifold chart seed
rules.input_form: topological space with compatible local charts
preconditions: Compatible smooth coordinate charts cover the space locally
rules.operation: Use compatible local Euclidean models to define a smooth manifold.
examples: The sphere is locally Euclidean even though it is not globally a Euclidean plane
counterexamples: Requiring a single global chart for every manifold is invalid

rules.name: Tangent vector seed
rules.input_form: smooth curve or derivation at a point
preconditions: The point and local smooth structure are fixed
rules.operation: Represent tangent vectors through curve velocities or derivations.
examples: Curve velocities give coordinate realizations of tangent vectors
counterexamples: Treating a point itself as a tangent vector is invalid

rules.name: Riemannian metric rule
rules.input_form: smooth assignment g_p on tangent spaces
preconditions: Each g_p is a positive-definite bilinear form varying smoothly in p
rules.operation: Use smooth positive-definite inner products on tangent spaces to define a Riemannian metric.
examples: The Euclidean dot product defines the standard metric on Euclidean space
counterexamples: An indefinite bilinear form is not a Riemannian metric

rules.name: Geodesic seed
rules.input_form: curve on a Riemannian manifold
preconditions: A Riemannian metric and its Levi-Civita connection are fixed
rules.operation: Characterize geodesics as locally extremizing curves or connection-straight curves.
examples: Straight lines in Euclidean space are geodesics of the standard metric
counterexamples: Arbitrary smooth curves are not geodesics in general

rules.name: Gaussian curvature seed
rules.input_form: smooth surface with metric data
preconditions: A surface metric or equivalent smooth geometric structure is fixed
rules.operation: Use intrinsic surface data to determine Gaussian curvature.
examples: The sphere has positive Gaussian curvature while the plane has zero Gaussian curvature
counterexamples: Confusing intrinsic curvature with arbitrary extrinsic bending is invalid

rules.name: Differential form degree rule
rules.input_form: k-form
rules.output_form: alternating covariant tensor field of degree k
preconditions: A smooth manifold and tensor conventions are fixed
rules.operation: Classify differential forms by alternating covariant degree.
examples: 1-forms act on tangent vectors, while 2-forms act on ordered tangent-vector pairs antisymmetrically
counterexamples: Treating a scalar field as a 1-form without an explicit differential or covector identification is invalid

rules.name: Exterior derivative nilpotence rule
rules.input_form: differential form omega
preconditions: The exterior derivative is taken in the standard smooth setting
rules.operation: Apply the nilpotence of the exterior derivative.
examples: Exact forms are automatically closed because applying d twice yields zero
counterexamples: Expecting d(d omega) to produce higher-order correction terms is invalid in exterior calculus

rules.name: Wedge antisymmetry rule
rules.input_form: forms alpha and beta of degrees p and q
rules.output_form: alpha wedge beta = (-1)^(pq) beta wedge alpha
preconditions: The wedge product is defined for the given forms
rules.operation: Swap forms in a wedge product with graded sign control.
examples: Swapping two 1-forms introduces a minus sign in the wedge product
counterexamples: Treating wedge multiplication as ordinary commutative multiplication is invalid

rules.name: Stokes theorem seed on manifolds
rules.input_form: oriented manifold with boundary and differential form omega
preconditions: The standard smoothness, orientation, and boundary hypotheses hold
rules.operation: Convert an integral of an exterior derivative over a manifold into a boundary integral.
examples: Manifold boundary integrals convert exterior derivatives into boundary flux terms through Stokes-type identities
counterexamples: Applying Stokes theorem without orientation or boundary regularity is invalid

rules.name: Covariant derivative component rule
rules.input_form: tensor field in local coordinates
preconditions: A connection and coordinate chart are fixed
rules.operation: Compute covariant derivatives in coordinates by correcting partial derivatives with connection coefficients.
examples: Vector-field derivatives on curved manifolds require connection terms beyond ordinary coordinate differentiation
counterexamples: Dropping Christoffel-symbol terms in nonflat coordinates is invalid in general

rules.name: Ricci curvature contraction seed
rules.input_form: Riemann curvature tensor
preconditions: A curvature tensor and contraction convention are fixed
rules.operation: Obtain Ricci curvature by tracing the Riemann tensor over a standard index pair.
examples: Curvature tensors reduce to Ricci data by tracing over appropriate indices
counterexamples: Arbitrary index contractions do not all define the Ricci tensor

rules.name: Jacobi field seed
rules.input_form: vector field along a geodesic
rules.output_form: Jacobi equation under geodesic variation hypotheses
preconditions: A Riemannian manifold, geodesic, and curvature operator are fixed
rules.operation: Model first-order geodesic variation through the Jacobi equation.
examples: Nearby geodesic families induce vector fields governed by curvature through the Jacobi equation
counterexamples: Arbitrary vector fields along a geodesic are not automatically Jacobi fields

rules.name: Sectional curvature rule
rules.input_form: two-plane in a tangent space
preconditions: Metric and Riemann curvature data are fixed
rules.operation: Assign a curvature scalar to a tangent two-plane using the Riemann tensor and metric.
examples: Constant-curvature manifolds assign the same sectional curvature to every tangent two-plane
counterexamples: Ricci curvature alone does not determine every sectional curvature value in general

rules.name: Lie derivative seed
rules.input_form: tensor field and vector field flow
rules.output_form: infinitesimal tensor variation along the flow
preconditions: A tensor field and generating vector field are fixed
rules.operation: Measure infinitesimal change of a tensor field along a vector-field flow.
examples: Symmetries are detected by vanishing Lie derivatives of the preserved tensor quantities
counterexamples: Replacing flow-based transport by ordinary coordinate differentiation is invalid in general

rules.name: Hodge star seed
rules.input_form: k-form on an oriented Riemannian manifold
preconditions: Metric and orientation data are fixed
rules.operation: Map differential forms to complementary-degree forms using the Hodge star.
examples: The Hodge star converts exterior-form data into dual-volume data tied to the metric
counterexamples: Defining the Hodge star without metric and orientation data is invalid in general

rules.name: de Rham cohomology bridge seed
rules.input_form: closed differential forms modulo exact forms
preconditions: The standard smooth-manifold and exterior-calculus setting is active
rules.operation: Convert closed-versus-exact differential-form structure into cohomological invariants.
examples: Exterior calculus yields topological invariants when closed forms are quotiented by exact forms
counterexamples: Treating every closed form as exact is invalid in general

rules.name: Canonical form normalization expansion
rules.input_form: raw expression E
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Rewrite expressions into a canonical form that preserves the active equivalence relation.
examples: x + y and y + x map to a shared canonical additive form in commutative settings
counterexamples: Applying canonicalization rules outside their preconditions is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions
